section.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on this, the beginning of speech from the Tent of Meeting was about the portion of offerings, because the revelation of Torah is primarily in the laws of offerings, and this is connected to the second day of Nissan when Natanel ben Tzu'ar offered, as the tribe of Yissachar knew Torah and advised the princes to volunteer these offerings.
section.t: And based on this, we can explain that the beginning of speech from the Tent of Meeting was the portion of offerings, because the revelation of Torah is primarily in the laws of offerings
(as above, section 1),
for it is through the offerings that the refinement of the world is accomplished,
and also that through them is the sustenance of the world,
this is through the power of Torah,
"When a man brings an offering" — this is Torah.
And we can connect this with the second day of Nissan,
on which Natanel ben Tzu'ar, prince of Yissachar, offered,
for the fact that he merited to offer second among the tribes is because the sons of Yissachar were knowledgeable in Torah, and because they advised the princes to volunteer these offerings.
For it can be said that these two matters are dependent on each other,
for because they were knowledgeable in Torah,
and the revelation of Torah is in the matter of offerings,
therefore they advised to volunteer offerings.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: One must understand how the revelation of Torah can be in the matter of offerings, which involve the refinement and sustenance of the world, when Torah is above the world and all worlds are insignificant before it.
section.t: And one must understand,
behold, Torah is above the world,
and as explained in Tanya
that Dovid was punished for calling words of Torah "songs,"
because Dovid was praising Torah in that all worlds depend on one detail of the details of Torah,
and he was punished for this,
for regarding Torah,
since it is united with Ein Sof, blessed be He,
all worlds are not really significant,
and it is not applicable that the revelation of Torah is in the matter of offerings, which are the refinement and sustenance of the world.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The explanation is that Torah as it is in itself is above worlds, but from the perspective of its root in the Awtsmoos, since He is not defined by any limitation, His desire for a dwelling in the lower worlds causes worldly matters to have a place in Torah, and Dovid's praise was valid from that root perspective.
section.t: And the explanation of this can be said,
that this — that Torah is above worlds — is Torah as it is in its own essence.
But from the perspective of the root of Torah as it is rooted in the Awtsmoos,
since His essential Self, blessed be He, is not defined, Heaven forbid, by any definition,
not even by this — that all worlds are insignificant before Him,
behold, through His desire to have a dwelling place in the lower worlds,
that He should have gratification and delight from the service of the lower ones,
it is thus also in Torah,
that worldly matters occupy a place, so to speak, regarding Torah.
And based on this, we can explain that Dovid was praising Torah in that the sustenance of all worlds depends on one detail of the details of Torah,
even though Torah is above worlds,
for from the perspective of the root of Torah as it is rooted in the Awtsmoos,
in that He desired to have a dwelling place in the lower worlds and that the dwelling in the lower worlds be through Torah,
this — that the life-force of all worlds depends on one detail of Torah — is the praise of Torah, so to speak.
[And that he was punished for this is because praise pertains to revelation,
and from the perspective of the revelation of Torah,
all worlds are not significant].
